blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

blocks.text:
**Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding
`localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON
override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run <config_file> <override>` deep-merges
`<override>` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into
`params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring
the same shape as the job config file itself:

```bash
dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}'
```

A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper)
is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the
unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its
normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed.

With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if
it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through
`scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true`
are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out
of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job
runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an
opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change.

**Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/
`forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via
`bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP
tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands
(`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) —
`bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with
`Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params`
therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session

`scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session,
throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual
`dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a
session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target
directory already exists).

```bash
warmup-session.sh --repo <git-url> --dir <target-dir> [--branch <name>] \
  [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"]
```

1. Delegation test: bug leg calls the shared gate exactly once with `(ticketKey, customParams, '', false, '')` and does NOT invoke feedbackLoop directly from the bug module.

Hmm, how to prove "does NOT invoke feedbackLoop directly"? The real feedbackLoop inside the gate is the one making the wrapper call. If the bug leg ALSO called feedbackLoop.resumeOnceForMissingResponse directly, there'd be TWO wrapper invocations (the gate's + the direct one) — except the attempt marker makes the second a no-op (attempts-exhausted, `attempted: false`, no command). Hmm — actually the direct call would then return without invoking (exactly-once marker). So the wrapper count stays 1 either way. 

Better discriminator: spy on the realFeedbackLoop instance passed to the BUG module. Since the gate and the bug module share the same feedbackLoop instance, I can't just count its calls. Alternative: give the bug module a DIFFERENT (spy) feedbackLoop instance from the one inside the shared-gate developTicket instance! The bug module's `./common/feedbackLoop.js` mapping doesn't have to be the same object as the developTicket instance's. That's actually the cleanest proof:

- `gateFeedbackLoop` = real feedbackLoop instance (shared file/cli mocks) — inside developTicketSharedGate.
- `bugFeedbackLoop` = a spy object `{ resumeOnceForMissingResponse: function(o) { directCalls.push(o); return { attempted: false, reason: 'spied-direct-call' }; }` — passed as `./common/feedbackLoop.js` to developBugAndCreatePR.

Then:
- Test "routes through the shared gate": directCalls.length === 0 (bug leg never calls feedbackLoop directly) AND recoverCalls deep-equals `[['TS-50', customParams, '', false, '']]` AND wrapper count === 1 (the gate's real resume fired).
- AC6 (bug) test: override the gate to throw the fatal marked error; assert the error propagates out of the bug action() with `fatalCliEnvironment === true`, no partial-work push, no comment/move.

Wait — for the fatal propagation test, use `opts.recoverMissingResponseImpl` that throws:
```js
var err = new Error('Fatal CLI/environment failure: cursor-agent not found in PATH');
err.fatalCliEnvironment = true;
throw err;
```
Then the bug leg's outer catch rethrows it (marker match). Assert caught.fatalCliEnvironment === true, no 'git push' commands, comments empty (no interrupted comment, no error comment — wait, the outer catch rethrows BEFORE posting '❌ Bug Development Error'? Let me re-check: the catch first checks markers and rethrows — yes, `if (error && (error.fatalCliEnvironment || ...)) { throw error; }` comes first, so no error comment. moves/removed empty too.

Hmm — but wait: is propagating the fatal error out of the bug pre-check the DESIRED behavior? Yes — AC6 semantics: the fatal class fails the job explicitly (red run), never a retry loop. The bug leg's outer catch rethrows marked fatalCliEnvironment errors. 

But hold on — with the REAL gate and empty signals ('' / false), isFatalCliEnvironmentError('', false) → false, so the fatal branch can't fire through the real gate from the bug leg today. The AC6-bug test uses an override impl to pin the CONTRACT: whatever the shared gate decides (including fatal), the bug leg obeys and never preempts/resumes around it. That's the drift-proofing the reviewer asked for.

Also — should the bug leg pass its own signals if it has them? The bug pre-check path doesn't compute CLI outcome signals (response text lives in params.response... hmm wait — actually, does the bug leg have `params.response` available at the pre-check? Yes! Teammate passes the CLI response as params.response. Hmm, could we pass `params.response` as developmentSummary to the gate so the text heuristics (exit 127 / not found in PATH / unknown provider) apply on the bug pre-check too?

Let me check what the bug post-action receives: `action(params)` — params.response would be the raw CLI output (if skipAIProcessing, the raw response). In the story leg, `developmentSummary` is presumably a derived summary of the response. Let me check what developmentSummary is in developTicketAndCreatePR (line ~895 area).

- `cliHasFatalError` → `actualParams.currentCliHasFatalError === true`.
- `cliErrorMessage` → `actualParams.currentCliErrorMessage || null`.

therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a
thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader`
in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo.

**Dev-leg whitelist (`story_development.json` / `bug_development.json`):** both
development legs set `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS":
"find,ls,cat,mkdir,bash,run-agent.sh,gradlew"}` at the job level. The `bash`
entry is deliberate and load-bearing, not copy-paste: the gh-775 missing-response
resume re-invokes the agent wrapper as
`bash -c "timeout -k 60 <N> bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <prompt>"`
through `cli_execute_command`, which whitelists the command's **first token** —
without `bash` the bounded resume (and the pre-existing feedback-loop resumes,
which also shell out through `bash`) could never run on these legs. Accepted
tradeoff, stated explicitly: whitelisting `bash` lets the agent execute arbitrary
commands via `bash -c`, so the first-token whitelist is no longer a command
boundary on this leg. That is accepted for the dev automation legs — the agent
already holds full write access to the working tree and its commands are logged —
but a config copied from these legs into a more restricted agent must re-make
that decision consciously.

entry is deliberate and load-bearing, not copy-paste: the gh-775 missing-response
resume re-invokes the agent wrapper as
`bash -c "timeout -k 60 <N> bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <prompt>"`
through `cli_execute_command`, which whitelists the command's **first token** —
without `bash` the bounded resume (and the pre-existing feedback-loop resumes,
which also shell out through `bash`) could never run on these legs. Accepted
tradeoff, stated explicitly: whitelisting `bash` lets the agent execute arbitrary
commands via `bash -c`, so the first-token whitelist is no longer a command
boundary on this leg. That is accepted for the dev automation legs — the agent
already holds full write access to the working tree and its commands are logged —
but a config copied from these legs into a more restricted agent must re-make
that decision consciously.

**Dev-leg whitelist (`story_development.json` / `bug_development.json`):** both
development legs set `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS":
"find,ls,cat,mkdir,bash,run-agent.sh,gradlew"}` at the job level. The `bash`
entry is deliberate and load-bearing, not copy-paste: the gh-775 missing-response
resume re-invokes the agent wrapper as
`bash -c "timeout -k 60 <N> bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <prompt>"`
through `cli_execute_command`, which whitelists the command's **first token** —
without `bash` the bounded resume (and the pre-existing feedback-loop resumes,
which also shell out through `bash`) could never run on these legs. Accepted
tradeoff, stated explicitly: whitelisting `bash` lets the agent execute arbitrary
commands via `bash -c`, so the first-token whitelist is no longer a command
boundary on this leg. That is accepted for the dev automation legs — the agent
already holds full write access to the working tree and its commands are logged —
but a config copied from these legs into a more restricted agent must re-make
that decision consciously.

resume re-invokes the agent wrapper as
`bash -c "timeout -k 60 <N> bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <prompt>"`
through `cli_execute_command`, which whitelists the command's **first token** —
without `bash` the bounded resume (and the pre-existing feedback-loop resumes,
which also shell out through `bash`) could never run on these legs. Accepted
tradeoff, stated explicitly: whitelisting `bash` lets the agent execute arbitrary
commands via `bash -c`, so the first-token whitelist is no longer a command
boundary on this leg. That is accepted for the dev automation legs — the agent
already holds full write access to the working tree and its commands are logged —
but a config copied from these legs into a more restricted agent must re-make
that decision consciously.

runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

content.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'

runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

blocks.text:
name: Agent Docs

# Mandatory check for PRs that touch agent configs, JS actions, instructions,
# prompts or human docs:
#   1. Regenerates docs/agents/generated/* and fails when the committed docs
#      are stale (git diff non-empty).
#   2. Runs the docs unit tests (agentDocGenerator + docs coverage) via dmtools.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'
      - '.github/workflows/agent-docs.yml'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - '*.json'
      - 'js/**'
      - 'instructions/**'
      - 'prompts/**'
      - 'docs/agents/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  docs-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Regenerate agent docs
        run: node js/agentDocGenerator.js

      - name: Fail when generated docs are stale
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated; then
            echo "::error::docs/agents/generated is stale. Run 'node js/agentDocGenerator.js' and commit the result."
            exit 1
          fi

  docs-coverage-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
